products.title: Ethiopia Miriga Village Washed
products.body_html:
C72: 

Farm/Producer: Miriga Village, Murgo Factory

Region: Ethiopia, Bensa, Sidama

Process: Washed

Altitude: 2400 - 2490 masl

Variety: 74158

Cup Profile: Grapefruit, Stone Fruits, Maple Syrup

Background info

We're excited to continue our relationship with Alo Coffee for a second consecutive year. After tasting through this season's offerings, the Ethiopia Miriga Village Washed stood out for its balance, clarity and the way it showcases everything we love about washed Ethiopian coffees. It's a coffee that's approachable yet expressive, making it just as enjoyable as a daily brew as it is something to slow down and appreciate.

Behind Alo Coffee are Tamiru Tadesse and his wife, Messi, who have quickly become some of Ethiopia's most respected coffee producers. Their first-ever Cup of Excellence entry in 2021 took first place, immediately putting Alo Coffee on the world stage. Since then, they've continued to invest in quality, expanding their network of washing stations while working closely with hundreds of smallholder farmers throughout Sidama. g

This lot comes from Miriga Village and is processed at the Murgo Washing Station. Ripe cherries are hand-picked and carefully sorted before being depulped. The coffee is then fermented in water to remove the remaining fruit before being thoroughly washed. Finally, it's dried slowly on raised African beds, where it's turned regularly to ensure even drying. This careful washing process highlights the coffee's natural clarity, sweetness, and vibrant citrus character.

In the cup, we found layers of stone fruits, think white peach and apricot, followed by bright citrus notes of grapefruit, mandarin, and bergamot. The washed process keeps the finish clean and crisp. With milk, those citrus notes soften and give way to a rich maple syrup sweetness, making for a surprisingly balanced and enjoyable milk coffee.

products.title: Colombia El Puente Natural
products.body_html:
C73: 

Farm/Producer: El Puente Mill

Region: Colombia, Huila, Palestina

Process: Natural

Altitude: 1680 masl

Variety: Caturra, Colombia, Castillo, Bourbon

Cup Profile: Melon, Plum, Strawberry Whirls

Background info

It’s Colombia season all year round. And we have the pleasure of showcasing a coffee we hold very close to our hearts. El Puente was one of the first lots we ever brought into Cedar, helping kick off the journey we’re still on today. So being able to bring it back year after year feels pretty wholesome. Somehow, it just seems to get better every time.

El Puente; meaning bridge takes its name from the footbridge crossing the river near the El Puente processing facility in Palestina, southern Huila. The facility works with coffee from more than 100 smallholder families in the surrounding area, allowing producers to process and deliver their coffee at a scale that wouldn’t be possible on their individual farms.

Once the cherries arrive, they’re floated to remove impurities and then assessed for Brix levels. Coffees with lower Brix are fermented in sacks for 12–24 hours before drying, while cherries with good Brix levels head straight to the drying stage.

This coffee has always been a bomb of flavour. In the cup, we’re getting loads of tropical fruit watermelon and cantaloupe are the first things that jump out. On espresso, those juicy fruit notes carry through, with dark plum adding a deeper layer. On milk think strawberry whirls,  sweet, fruity and ridiculously easy to drink.

products.title: Kenya Thunguri AB Washed
products.body_html:
C70: 

Farm/Producer: Rumukia Co-operative, Thunguri Factory

Region: Kenya, Nyeri-Mukurwe-ini

Process: Washed

Altitude: 1750 - 1900 masl

Variety: SL28, SL34, Batian

Cup Profile: Caramelized Sugar, Blackcurrant, Crunchie Biscuit

 

Background info: 

This lot immediately stood out as the kind of Kenyan coffee we’ve loved for years; classic, expressive, and unmistakably Nyeri. It has that familiar structure and clarity, with a vibrant acidity that feels intentional rather than aggressive.

Thunguri meaning “a hill” in Kikuyu is produced by small-scale farmers delivering to the Thunguri Factory, part of the Rumukia Co-operative Society in Nyeri’s Mukurwe-ini region. Established in 1961, the factory has long been a collective effort to improve livelihoods through coffee.

This coffee follows a traditional Kenyan washed process with a carefully managed double fermentation. After pulping, the coffee undergoes an initial fermentation, is washed, and then returned for a second stage.The process is closely monitored, with regular turning to ensure even fermentation. After washing and grading, the coffee is rested under shade before being dried on raised beds over 14–21 days, allowing the profile to fully stabilise.

On espresso and filter, this coffee shows a vibrant blackcurrant character with bright citrus bringing lift and structure. As it opens up, a caramelised sugar sweetness rounds everything out, giving the cup balance and depth. In milk, it shifts into something softer and more nostalgic, reminiscent of a Crunchie biscuit,sweet, lightly honeyed, and still lively enough to carry through.

products.title: Kenya Kiamwangi Natural
products.body_html:
C71: 

Farm/Producer: Iriaini Co-operative, Kiamwangi Factory

Region: Kenya, Nyeri, Mathira

Process: Natural

Altitude: 1700 - 1900 masl

Variety: SL28, SL34, Batian

Cup Profile: Mango, Tropical fruit juice, King Cone ice cream

Background info

Kenyan coffees have long been celebrated for their vibrant acidity and remarkable complexity, but naturally processed Kenyan coffees remain relatively uncommon. When we cupped this lot, it offered everything we love about Kenya but with the added richness and intensity that natural processing brings.

This coffee comes from Kiamwangi Factory, part of the Iriaini Farmers' Cooperative Society in the Mathira region of Nyeri, Kenya. The Iriaini Cooperative supports over 1,100 farmers, each cultivating small plots on the fertile volcanic slopes of Mount Kenya.

The farmers grow a mix of Kenya's renowned SL28 and SL34 varieties alongside the newer Ruiru 11 and Batian cultivars. Many producers also practice intercropping and sustainable farming methods that help improve soil health and biodiversity.

Unlike the traditional washed coffees that Kenya is famous for, this lot undergoes an innovative natural process. Only fully ripe cherries are carefully hand-selected before being sealed in food-grade fermentation bags. The cherries ferment for approximately 72 hours in a controlled low-oxygen environment, encouraging greater fruit complexity while carefully managing microbial activity. Following fermentation, the cherries are transferred to raised drying beds where they are regularly turned under the sun until reaching a stable moisture content of around 10%. 

On both filter and espresso, this coffee showcases ripe mango and vibrant tropical fruit juice, delivering this juicy sweetness. The acidity is bright and refreshing, balanced by a silky body and a clean, lingering finish. With milk, the fruit softens into a creamy dessert-like sweetness, rich vanilla ice cream wrapped in a cone chocolate shell reminiscent of a King Cone ice cream.

products.title: Costa Rica La Isla SL28 Natural
products.body_html:
C69: 

Farm/Producer: La Isla, Jiménez and Padilla family

Region: Costa Rica, Naranjo, Lourdes

Process: Natural

Altitude: 1560 masl

Variety: SL28

Cup Profile: Cling Peach, Rooibos, Caramel Cake

 

Background info: 

We’re always looking for coffees that clearly express place, variety and processing, and this lot from La Isla is a great continuation of that. Having worked with this producer before, we were excited to see how SL28 performs on the farm. It stood out for its structure and clarity, bringing a more vibrant, fruit-forward profile while still holding that balanced, sweet character we’ve come to expect from La Isla.

La Isla is a young, fast-rising farm in Naranjo, run by the Jiménez & Padilla family, and already making its mark with a 6th place in the 2024 Cup of Excellence Costa Rica. Grown at 1500–1700 MASL, this SL28 benefits from the region’s volcanic soils and stable climate, offering a slightly different expression of a varietal more commonly associated with Kenya.

This lot is processed as a natural, with cherries handpicked at peak ripeness and dried slowly in their whole form. The result is a more fruit-driven and syrupy profile, while still maintaining clarity in the cup.

On filter, expect a bright, juicy cup with notes of cling peach and a clean, structured acidity. As espresso, the profile becomes more rounded and syrupy, with rooibos-like notes coming through. With milk, it softens into a smooth, dessert-like cup, with a caramel cake sweetness.

products.title: Rwanda Vunga Washed
products.body_html:
C68: 

Farm/Producer: Vunga Washing Station

Region: Rwanda, Nyabihu District

Process: Washed

Altitude: 1450 - 1600 masl

Variety: Red Bourbon

Cup profile: Nectarines, Pineapple, Biscoff

 

Background info: 

This marks the third time we’re sharing Rwanda Vunga with you and if you’ve been with us since the early days, you’ll recognise it as one of the very first coffees we ever released. Returning to this lot feels meaningful for us, and we’re proud to showcase the latest harvest from this remarkable cooperative once again.

Vunga Cooperative is a small but vibrant community of farmers dedicated to producing high-quality coffee. Led by President Uwimana Daphrose, the cooperative has formed a partnership with Muraho Trading Co, which provides export and financing capabilities to help them increase their quality and reach new markets.

This cooperative showcases the unique terroir of Rwanda. The coffee is grown, harvested, and processed with care, resulting in a complex and nuanced flavour profile. The processing method involves washing, fermentation in concrete tanks, and drying in parchment, which brings out the coffee's distinct characteristics.

This coffee offers a distinct flavour profile depending on the brewing method. As a filter, it opens up with vibrant notes of nectarine and pineapple, carried by a juicy acidity and a clean, expressive finish. As an espresso, it presents a more concentrated profile; ripe stonefruit sweetness with bright tropical acidity. In milk-based drinks we picked up notes of Biscoff smooth texture with a sweet finish.

products.title: Colombia | Decaf CO2
products.body_html:
D003

Process: Carbon Dioxide

Cup Profile: Brazil Nut, Marzipan, Butterscotch

Background info:

It's been a long time coming but its finally here, our latest decaf lot. This time we working with a CO2 decaffeinated Colombian Coffee, just so you know this decaf is chemical-free. Here is a little background information on how this coffee is decaffeinated:

The green coffee is soaked in fresh hot water which allows the coffee beans to expand and become porous. It is then placed into a sealed vessel where it gets pressurized with liquid CO2. The CO2 then dissolves the caffeine from the beans. This mixture is then removed from the beans, where they will undergo a drying phase to finish off the process.

This process is the least invasive method of removing caffeine without changing the flavour profile of the coffee. We picked up notes of Brazil Nuts on both our filter brew and espresso. The espresso does however have a sweeter note of Marzipan which sticks to the theme of nuts very well. This all transforms our milk beverage into this butterscotch sweetness, the closest you'll get to us serving a Butterscotch Latte.

products.title: Cedar Seasonal Blend
products.body_html:
B017

Process: Washed and Natural

Altitude: 1100 - 2000 masl

Blend components: Brazil, Tanzania, Guatemala

Cup Profile: Balanced, Sweet, Pecan Nuts & Milk Chocolate.

Background info:

This is our signature blend where we aim to achieve a consistent flavour profile that provides a good balance of sweetness and body. Roast profile suits espresso-based drinks with its toned down acidity and smooth mouthfeel. A perfect coffee for the morning and everyday use. We prefer using this coffee for brewers that exemplify full body and bold notes such as espresso, plunger and moka-pots. Coffee is seasonal so expect our components to change throughout the year but maintain a consistent flavour profile.

products.title: Milky Way Blend
products.body_html:
B014

Process: Washed and Natural

Altitude: 1100 - 1400 masl

Blend components: Brazil, Guatemala

Cup Profile: Milk Chocolate, Toasted Nut Finish

Background info:

This blend came about through client feedback and quite a lot of roasting and tasting. We found that people enjoyed milk with their coffee and sometimes quite a lot of it. The one thing we always aim to achieve is balance and sweetness. We introduce to you our Milky Way Blend. This is designed for all you milk lovers and mug drinkers.

Our aim was simply to produce a flavour profile that can hold good sweetness and cut through all that milk. This blend has also been designed for bean-to-cup machines you would typically find at your workplace. Although it's meant for milk, it still packs quite a punch with heavier flavour tones. Perfect for Espresso and Moka pot as well.

products.title: Cedar Milky Way Compostable Pods
products.body_html:
Our aim at Cedar has always been to make coffee more accessible; wanting everyone to drink better coffee. In order to do this we needed to explore all forms of coffee brewing. 

One such brewing we finally tapped into was coffee pods, it's been a long time coming but for good reason. We decided to work on this project with 4WKS to produce a 100% compostable coffee pod. We didn't want to make a pod just for the sake of it; we needed to understand the nuances of pod brewing and match it with a suitable coffee offering. 

So we decided on our Milky Way blend for its flavour profile and how well it holds up in pod brewing. There is an option of 10 or 50 pods per box and they are compatible with Nespresso capsule machines as well as the premium Morning machines. We decided to go one step further and create a few recipes for you guys to use with our specific pods. Keep your eyes on our socials as we roll them out through the coming weeks.
